# Chuck & Co. Pet Care

> Locally owned dog walking and pet sitting in Eugene, Oregon.

Services: Dog Walking, Drop-In Visits, Overnight Pet Sitting, Puppy Visits, Pet Taxi, Adventure Hikes.
Service area: Downtown, Whiteaker, West University, Fairmount, Laurel Hill Valley, College Hill, Friendly Area, Jefferson Westside, South Eugene, Southeast Neighbors, Crest Drive, Southwest Hills, Churchill, Far West, Bethel, Trainsong, River Road, Santa Clara, Cal Young, Goodpasture Island, Ferry Street Bridge, Willakenzie, Harlow, Fox Hollow (Eugene, OR ZIPs 97401-97405, 97408).
Booking: free meet & greet via https://chuckandcopetcare.com/book

## Services
- [Dog Walking](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/services/dog-walking): Neighborhood walks with the same familiar walker, rain or shine.
- [Drop-In Visits](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/services/drop-in-visits): Quick, thorough check-ins for potty breaks, meals, meds and play.
- [Overnight Pet Sitting](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/services/overnight-pet-sitting): A trusted sitter stays in your home so your dog keeps their routine.
- [Puppy Visits](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/services/puppy-visits): Potty breaks, meals, play and gentle reinforcement for growing pups.
- [Pet Taxi](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/services/pet-taxi): Safe rides to the vet, groomer, daycare and back home.
- [Adventure Hikes](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/services/adventure-hikes): Leashed trail outings on Eugene’s best dog-friendly paths.

## Guides
- [Off-Leash Dog Areas in Eugene: A Local Guide](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/off-leash-dog-areas-eugene): Eugene has designated off-leash dog areas in several city parks, including Alton Baker Park, Amazon Park and Candlelight Park. Dogs must stay on leash everywhere else unless signs say otherwise. Check City of Eugene Parks for current hours and rules before you go.
- [Dog-Friendly Hikes In and Near Eugene](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/dog-friendly-hikes-near-eugene): Good leashed hikes for dogs in Eugene include the Ridgeline Trail system, Spencer Butte, Pre’s Trail in Alton Baker Park and the paths in Hendricks Park. Choose shaded trails in summer and bring water, a towel and a tick check routine.
- [Dog Licensing and Leash Rules in Eugene and Lane County](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/eugene-dog-licensing-and-leash-rules): Dogs in Lane County, including Eugene, generally need a county dog license and current rabies vaccination. Dogs should be leashed in public unless in a designated off-leash area. Rules change, so confirm details with Lane County Animal Services and the City of Eugene.
- [Walking Your Dog in Eugene’s Rainy Season](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/walking-your-dog-in-eugene-rain): Walk your dog through Eugene’s rainy season by using a reflective raincoat for short-coated dogs, choosing paved or bark routes over mud, shortening walks in downpours, and drying paws and ears afterward to prevent irritation.
- [Wildfire Smoke and Your Dog: When to Skip the Walk](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/wildfire-smoke-and-dogs): When air quality in Eugene reaches unhealthy levels, keep walks short, slow and close to home, and skip strenuous exercise. Seniors, puppies, short-snouted breeds and dogs with heart or lung issues are most at risk. Watch for coughing or labored breathing.
- [Summer Heat Safety for Eugene Dogs](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/summer-heat-safety-for-dogs): On hot Eugene days, walk your dog early in the morning or late in the evening, use shaded routes, carry water and test pavement with the back of your hand for seven seconds. Heavy panting, drooling or stumbling can signal heat stress.
- [Foxtails and Grass Seeds: A Summer Hazard for Oregon Dogs](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/foxtails-and-grass-seeds): Foxtails are barbed grass seeds common in Oregon summers that can work into a dog’s paws, ears, nose and eyes. Avoid dry, tall grass, check your dog after every walk and see a vet for sudden head shaking, sneezing, limping or squinting.
- [Ticks and Dogs in the Willamette Valley](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/ticks-and-dogs-willamette-valley): Ticks are present around Eugene, especially on trail edges and in tall grass during spring and early summer. Ask your vet about prevention, check your dog after hikes, and remove ticks promptly with fine tweezers or a tick tool.
- [What to Expect at Your First Meet & Greet](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/what-to-expect-meet-and-greet): A meet & greet is a free 20- to 30-minute visit in your home where we meet your dog, learn their routine, review keys and access, and answer your questions. There is no obligation to book.
- [How to Prepare for an Overnight Pet Sitter](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/preparing-for-an-overnight-pet-sitter): Before an overnight sitter arrives, leave written routines, enough food and medication for the full trip plus extra, your vet and emergency contacts, Wi-Fi and alarm details, and clear notes on any rules or quirks.
- [Puppy Potty Break Schedule by Age](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/puppy-potty-break-schedule): Many trainers suggest puppies can hold it about one hour per month of age, up to roughly four to five hours. A 3-month-old puppy may need a break every three hours, plus after meals, naps and play.
- [How Often Should You Walk Your Dog?](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/how-often-should-you-walk-your-dog): Most adult dogs benefit from at least two walks a day totaling 30 to 60 minutes, plus potty breaks. High-energy breeds may need more, while seniors and small breeds may do better with shorter, more frequent outings.
- [Questions to Ask Before Hiring a Dog Walker in Eugene](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/questions-to-ask-a-dog-walker): Before hiring a dog walker, ask who will actually walk your dog, how keys are handled, what happens in an emergency, how updates are sent, whether walks are private or group, and how weather, holidays and cancellations are handled.
- [Helping a Dog with Separation Anxiety](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/separation-anxiety-in-dogs): Signs of separation anxiety include barking, pacing, chewing near doors and accidents when left alone. Gradual practice, enrichment, consistent routines and midday visits can help. For moderate to severe cases, work with your vet or a qualified trainer.
- [Fireworks, Game Days and Noise Anxiety](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/fireworks-and-noise-anxiety): Help your dog through fireworks and loud events by walking earlier in the day, closing windows and curtains, playing background noise, offering a safe hiding spot and making sure ID tags and microchip info are current.
- [Booking Holiday Pet Sitting in Eugene](https://chuckandcopetcare.com/guides/holiday-pet-sitting-eugene): Book holiday pet sitting in Eugene three to six weeks ahead for Thanksgiving, winter holidays, spring break, UO graduation and major event weekends. Availability fills quickly, and early booking guarantees your preferred sitter.
